NEW DELHI: The Chamber of Trade and Industry on Saturday urged Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi to postpone the INDIA bloc's upcoming rally on November 1 at Ramlila Maidan, saying the demonstration could disrupt business worth Rs 10,000 crore during the peak Diwali shopping season.In a letter to Rahul, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said the rally could affect wholesale and retail markets around Ramlila Maidan at a time when traders expect heavy customer footfall ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali."This year, Dhanteras falls on Friday, November 6, Diwali on November 8 and Bhai Dooj on November 10. People begin shopping for Dhanteras and Diwali a week in advance. In Delhi alone, Dhanteras-related business across sectors such as gold and silver, utensils, electronics, textiles, dry fruits, sweets, automobiles, vehicles, property and gift items amounts to approximately Rs 25,000 crore. This trade is the backbone of Delhi's economy," the letter reads.The traders' body said markets generally see increased activity about a week before the festivals, making the timing of the rally a matter of concern.Goyal also said traders in Delhi had already suffered losses of around Rs 3,000 crore in October due to rallies, marches and road closures in Connaught Place, India Gate and central Delhi."According to CTI's estimates, traders in Delhi have already suffered losses of approximately Rs 3,000 crore due to repeated rallies, marches and road closures in Connaught Place, India Gate and central Delhi," he said."The movement of goods into wholesale markets had come to a halt, while retail customers were unable to reach the markets," he added.The organisation also pointed to around 20 wholesale and retail markets within a five-kilometre radius of Ramlila Maidan, including Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Kashmere Gate, Nai Sarak, Mori Gate, Kinari Bazar, Dariba, Daryaganj, Ajmeri Gate, Jama Masjid, Karol Bagh and Azad Market."Goods from these markets are supplied across the country. Traffic diversions, metro station closures and barricading during the rally could bring business in these markets to a complete standstill," Goyal said.While acknowledging the right to peaceful protest and democratic expression, CTI urged political parties to avoid holding large rallies in key commercial areas until the festival period ends.The opposition rally aims to ramp up pressure on the government over the "vote chori" issue and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.On October 12, protests over the "vote theft" charge reached the Supreme Court's doorstep, with opposition leaders, activists and civil society members participating in a 'March for Democracy' along a heavily barricaded route in Delhi and filing a joint petition against the SIR.Rahul hosted INDIA bloc leaders for tea at his home on October 13. After the meeting, the opposition bloc vowed to continue resisting and take the "vote chori" fight to its logical conclusion.
Article Summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry urged Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi to postpone the INDIA bloc's upcoming rally on November 1. The demonstration could disrupt business worth Rs 10,000 crore during the peak Diwali shopping season. The rally aims to ramp up pressure on the government over the "vote chori" issue.

Article Title: After Operation Sindoor friction, Delhi & Baku reset ties with EAM Jaishankar's visit
Article Text:
EAM S Jaishankar and his counterpart Jeyhun Bayramov agreed to expand cooperation.

NEW DELHI: Amid ongoing efforts by both India and Azerbaijan for a reset in ties, EAM S Jaishankar and his counterpart Jeyhun Bayramov agreed to expand cooperation in energy, trade, investment and connectivity in a “very productive” meeting in Baku.Jaishankar’s visit to Azerbaijan was the first by an Indian foreign minister in eight years and built upon the diplomatic goodwill created by PM Modi’s meeting with Azerbaijan President Ilham Aliyev on the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek last month.Ties between the two countries had been held back by geopolitical reasons for a while, mainly Azerbaijan’s ties with Pakistan — as evident from its support for Islamabad after Op Sindoor last year — and India’s defence ties with Armenia.While Bayramov spoke about taking the relationship to a higher level, setting aside past differences, Jaishankar underlined the significance of trade and energy cooperation. Terrorism was also among the issues discussed. “We spoke about economic cooperation, including trade, investment and energy, which are central to our bilateral ties... We believe there is very good scope for further enhancement of bilateral trade and investment.We also discussed various activities and exchanges,” said Jaishankar.“We spoke about connectivity because it is so important in a globalised economy,” he said, adding that they agreed to coordinate more closely on the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).The EAM also called on Aliyev in Baku. “Discussed strengthening relationship between our two countries. Appreciate his positive sentiments for this shared endeavour,” he said.Jaishankar welcomed peace agreement between Azerbaijan and Armenia, expressing hope that it would lead to the establishment of a durable peace.
Article Summary: Jaishankar’s visit to Azerbaijan was the first by an Indian foreign minister in eight years. Ties between the two countries had been held back by geopolitical reasons for a while. Terrorism was also among the issues discussed in a ‘very productive’ meeting.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a first, govt has proposed mentioning the nationality of driving licence holders on DLs and introducing separate colour schemes for Indian andforeign nationals as well as doing away with affidavits sworn before an executive magistrate or notary as proof of age and address, which has the potential of being misused.Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposing sweeping changes to the driving licence (DL) regime under Motor Vehicles Rules, the road transport ministry Wednesday issued a draft notification to raise the pass mark for the online safe-driving tutorial assessment from the current 60% to 75%.It has also proposed making it mandatory for licences to carry the holder’s blood group, mobile number and emergency contact details. The ministry has proposed waiving fees for specified DL services, including changes to address, name and contact number, if applicants avail themselves of these services through online Aadhaar authentication.At present, if an applicant cannot produce any of the 12 listed documents, the licencing authority “may accept an affidavit sworn before an executive magistrate, judicial magistrate or notary public as proof of age and address”.Anil Chhikara, an expert in motor vehicle licencing, said, “The use of simple affidavits is being phased out after miscreants used them to register false addresses and dates of birth. Applicants must now provide verifiable documents. ”Under the draft, the ministry has listed separate sets of documents for proof of address, age and identity. Address proofs include Aadhaar card, Electoral Photo Identity Card, e-ration card, electricity or gas bills for the preceding three months, and proof of legal presence for foreign nationals. Acceptable age proofs include passports, school board mark sheets, birth certificates and identity cards issued by govt departments. Aadhaar, passports, e-ration cards and PAN have been listed as acceptable identity proofs.The proposed changes aim to curb the submission of false documents, tighten assessment requirements and make licence-related services more accessible. They also seek to streamline online DL services and set timelines for processing applications to change licence particulars.Under the proposal, the safe-driving tutorial would have to last at least 30 minutes, while the higher qualifying score of 75% is intended to make the assessment more stringent. Licencing authorities would have to approve or reject online applications to change DL particulars, including name and address, within 15 days, giving reasons for rejection.An application for a change of address that remains undecided for 30 days would be deemed approved. The draft also proposes a consolidated application form for services such as DL renewal, issuance of duplicate licences, addition of a vehicle class and changes to personal particulars. Specified applicant details would be retrieved electronically from the Sarathi portal wherever available.
Article Summary: Govt plans colour-coded DLs for Indians, foreigners. Life insurance policies, too, would no longer be accepted as proof. Proposed changes aim to curb the submission of false documents. They also seek to streamline online DL services and set timelines for processing applications.

Article Title: Cabinet secretariat merely acknowledged complaint of ECs against senior poll officer: RTI
Article Text:
The two ECs alleged the changes were made without prior discussion with the commission or officers concerned.

NEW DELHI: After election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi wrote to cabinet secretary TV Somanathan in July objecting to the revised allocation of work among senior commission officers by senior deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) Maneesh Garg without EC approval, the secretariat merely sent them an acknowledgement with a copy to CEC Gyanesh Kumar for information, an RTI reply has revealed.The senior officers among whom the work was reallocated by Garg, who was only filling in for DEC (administration) Bhanu Prakash Yeturu while he was on leave, included Seema Khanna, who was brought in as head of the IT division of EC. Sandhu and Joshi, according to a report in Indian Express dated Sept 23, had in internal notes to DEC concerned, alleged that the ECINET software conceived and managed by the IT division, was too centralised, blocking access to field officers who were authorised by law to make changes to the electoral roll.Explaining the rationale behind the reluctance to take any action, a confidential note on the file shared by the Cabinet secretariat with transparency activist, Commodore Lokesh K Batra (Retd), as part of its 21-page RTI reply, stated that EC being a Constitutional body is insulated from the Executive's interference by design."The...communications are from the ECs in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from the commission as a whole," it said adding that Garg is an officer of the EC and his work and conduct is to be regulated by rules and guidelines of EC."In the absence of any official communication from the commission as a whole, any action at this stage may be inappropriate. It may also be construed as interference in the functioning of the constitutional body," the note underlines before announcing the decision to merely send an acknowledgement to the two ECs, with copies marked to the CEC and the DoPT.Commodore Batra had on September 24 sought copies of the Commissioners' communications, details of the steps taken by the Cabinet Secretariat and the relevant file notings. This was a day after The Indian Express reported that two election commissioners had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps involving the addition of new voters and deletion of names from electoral rolls, and had approached the Cabinet Secretary over concerns about the integrity of the voter database.According to the documents shared as part of the RTI response, the two ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, wrote separate but near-identical letters to Cabinet Secretary TV Somanathan on July 29, 2026, objecting to the conduct of a Garg and an order he issued revising the allocation of work among senior officers. The two Commissioners alleged that the changes were made without prior discussion with the Commission or the officers concerned.A cabinet secretariat file noting dated Aug 3 says that both the ECs have stated that Garg, after assuming the charge as link officer of DEC (Administration), has issued an order regarding work allocation of equivalent and senior officers to him without discussing the revised work allocation with the Commission or the officers concerned.“Further, the ECs stated that this has happened despite repeated oral and written instructions to all concerned officers against taking such actions without prior discussion/approval of the Commission,” noting highlights.“In this connection, we may request the CEC for his opinion on the issue," it said.In another noting dated Aug 4, it is stated that the EC is a “Constitutional body and is insulated from executive interference by design to ensure that it functions independently and in a transparent manner. The working and functioning of the Commission are governed by the rules and guidelines of the Election Commission.”It further states that since the communications are from the ECs in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from the Commission as a whole.The noting also stated that although Maneesh Garg had been appointed by the ACC, he was now an officer of the ECI and his work and conduct is to be regulated and monitored by the rules and guidelines of ECI. It further stated that the ECs have sent these communications for appropriate action; however, in the absence of any official communication from the Commission as a whole, any action at this stage may be inappropriate. It may also be construed as interference in the functioning of the Constitutional Body. "Hence, it would be appropriate to send acknowledgement to both Election Commissioners with a copy to PPS to CEC for information of CEC," it stated.A copy was also marked to be sent to the secretary, department of personnel and training since Garg was an All-India Service officer.
Article Summary: Two election commissioners objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps involving the addition of new voters and deletion of names from electoral rolls. The secretariat merely sent them an acknowledgement with a copy to CEC Gyanesh Kumar for information. The two Commissioners alleged that the changes were made without prior discussion with the Commission or the officers concerned.

Article Title: Centre bans reuse of single-use medical devices across hospitals; flags recycling of disposables
Article Text:
Govt Flags Recycling Of Disposables In Critical Ops (Generative image)

The DGHS said that reuse could expose patients to cross-infection, device malfunction, reduced performance and other complications.

NEW DELHI: The Centre has directed public and private healthcare facilities across the country to strictly stop reusing medical devices and disposable surgical items meant for one-time use, flagging patient safety risks from the practice, particularly in critical care.In a letter dated Oct 16, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said it had come to its notice that some private and corporate hospitals were reusing single-use devices after sterilising them, including items used in cardiology, nephrology, oncology, cardiothoracic and vascular surgery (CTVS), neurosurgery and other clinical services.The DGHS said that reuse could expose patients to cross-infection, device malfunction, reduced performance and other complications. It said the practice could violate provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010, and applicable infection-control and biomedical waste management requirements.The directive calls on state health authorities and drug controllers to maintain strict vigilance, inspect and monitor healthcare establishments, and take action against violations under applicable laws and regulations.Devices labelled for single use must be used in accordance with the instructions and recommendations of the original equipment manufacturer.The letter, addressed to health authorities in states and Union Territories, the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) and the central govt health scheme (CGHS), also flagged cases in which patients were charged the full cost of devices that had been reused, or the cost was reimbursed by govt authorities.The DGHS said the CGHS had issued an office memorandum on the issue in Nov 2016 for hospitals empanelled under the scheme.Single-use devices reportedly reused in India include cardiac catheters and guidewires used in angiography and angioplasty, dialysis equipment, certain surgical instruments and disposable syringes and needles. Such practices raise concerns about infection risks and patient safety, particularly when patients are not informed.Welcoming the directive, the Association of Indian Medical Device Industry (AiMeD) said reuse of devices designed and validated for one-time use could put patients at risk. Its forum coordinator, Rajiv Nath, said enforcement should also clarify responsibility when a device is reused contrary to the manufacturer’s instructions.AiMeD called for regular inspections, traceable records of device use and disposal, staff training and action against violations. It also urged govt to ensure that cost does not become a reason for hospitals to reuse disposable devices.The directive places the responsibility for enforcement on state and UT authorities. However, the letter does not specify a new inspection schedule or a separate penalty for hospitals found reusing such devices.
Article Summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said it had come to its notice that some private and corporate hospitals were reusing single-use devices after sterilising them. The DGHS said that reuse could expose patients to cross- infection, device malfunction, reduced performance and other complications.

Article Title: Northwest India turned drier, south wetter over 70 years, finds IMD study
Article Text:
The findings, published in the IMD’s peer-reviewed journal Mausam.

‘Hot, dry zone pushed east into UP over past 70 years’

NEW DELHI: A new IMD study finds that northwest India has turned drier, with its dry climate zone expanding from about a quarter to one-third of the total geographical area, whereas the south peninsula became wetter due to a rise in overall quantitative rainfall over the past seven decades.The findings, published in the IMD’s peer-reviewed journal Mausam, note that the dry zone that once ended in western UP is now extending into the east of the state, with the scientists warning the change could affect paddy cultivation in the north.In northwest India, the hot semi-arid zone grew from about a quarter of the region’s area in 1951-1980 to a third in 1991-2020, while the temperate zone shrank from about a quarter to less than a fifth, meaning that an area equal to roughly 7% of the region moved into the drier zone as temperatures rose and rainfall declined, said the study.It said peninsular India, on the other hand, reported shrinking of its hot semi-arid zone from about 30% of the region to 16%, and most of that land moved into the tropical savannah zone, which now covers three-quarters of the peninsula, a change the authors attribute to rising rainfall over southern India.“Within these broader shifts, Marathwada and west Vidarbha in Maharashtra moved into the hot semi-arid zone, and the tropical monsoon zone extended along the Konkan coast, coastal Karnataka and Kerala,” said the study, conducted by scientists from IMD and Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology.“When we compared India’s climate map decade by decade from 1951 to 2020, the clearest change was in the north, where the hot, dry zone has pushed east into Uttar Pradesh, and because this is one of the country’s most important farming regions, the timing of sowing and harvesting there needs to be watched closely,” said Ananya Karmakar, the study’s lead author.Since the scientists highlight potential implications for agriculture and the need to track long-term climate shifts, the study could be handy for farm sector policymakers.
Article Summary: A new IMD study finds that northwest India has turned drier, with its dry climate zone expanding from about a quarter to one-third of the total geographical area. The south peninsula became wetter due to a rise in overall quantitative rainfall over the past seven decades. The study could be handy for farm sector policymakers.

Article Title: Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map
Article Text:
That atmospheric conditions regulate pollution levels was always known. (File photo)

Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The winter of 2022-23 was remarkably clean in north India with PM2.5 levels down by up to 30% from the average of the previous three years, while peninsular India was considerably dirtier, with average PM2.5 levels in Mumbai spiking by 45%. The next winter (2023-24), the pattern dramatically reversed: PM2.5 spiralled in the North, while falling sharply in peninsular India.What changed within a span of a year? The big difference, as per a new study, was that 2022-23 was a La Niña year, while El Niño prevailed in the subsequent winter.Coming ahead of India’s peak pollution season, the paper, titled ‘Air quality in flux: The baffling ENSO transition in India’, published in Atmospheric Pollution Research journal Thursday, found that La Niña/El Niño conditions altered atmospheric circulation, PM2.5 transport pathways and weather conditions that determine whether pollution disperses or gets trapped.That atmospheric conditions regulate pollution levels was always known. What the study shows is how the atmosphere in winters can behave very differently under El Nino and La Nina conditions, determining where pollutants accumulate and where they are carried away even when emissions remain broadly similar. However, the researchers caution that the study does not establish that El Niño invariably worsens air quality in Delhi or north India.“We are not implying that the 2023-24 El Niño pattern will be repeated this winter. The two years that we studied were unusual and unique,” said atmospheric scientist Gufran Beig, one of the study’s authors. “This year’s El Niño is likely to be the strongest on record.”The study found that during the La Niña winter of 2022-23, stronger winds over north India helped disperse emissions from stubble-burning and local sources. The altered circulation bypassed Delhi and its surroundings and transported these pollutants southwards towards peninsular India. This resulted in substantially higher PM2.5 levels in cities such as Mumbai and Thiruvananthapuram.The following winter, the atmospheric setup changed. Under El Niño, winds over northern India were weaker and passed through areas, including Delhi and Jaipur, rather than carrying pollutants away. The resulting stagnation favoured the accumulation of PM2.5. Jaipur, for instance, recorded an increase of about 50% compared with the 2019-22 average, while Delhi logged a spike of over 10%.Weather conditions also mattered differently in the two years. Rain can remove pollutants from air, while high pressure, weak winds and a shallow boundary layer can trap them close to the ground. In Jaipur, rainfall was more strongly associated with lower PM2.5 during 2022-23, whereas surface pressure became a more important factor during 2023-24, leading to pollution spikes after rain.The researchers also used backward air-mass trajectories to trace where the air reaching cities had travelled from. Jaipur continued to receive air from polluted northern regions during the El Niño winter. Hyderabad, by contrast, received more marine and southern air, helping explain why its pollution pattern moved in the opposite direction.Overall, the study found substantial year-to-year PM2.5 variations from average levels in 2019-22 — ranging from about a 40% decline to a 70% increase, despite no major changes in emissions or pollution-control policies during the period. The authors underlined that the correlations neither establish direct causation nor can these be extrapolated to other years.For Delhi-NCR, this has an important implication: relatively low local or agricultural emissions do not automatically guarantee cleaner air if large-scale circulation turns stagnant. Conversely, even substantial emissions can have a smaller local impact when strong winds efficiently disperse or divert them.The winter pollution story may begin in Delhi and its neighbourhood, but increasingly, the weather that decides its intensity is being written on a much larger canvas.
Article Summary: Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map in India. The winter of 2022-23 was remarkably clean in north India with PM2.5 levels down by up to 30% from the average of the previous three years. The next winter (2023-24), the pattern dramatically reversed: PM 2.5 spiralled in the North, while falling sharply in peninsular India.

Article Title: India highlights nuclear advances, development partnerships at UNGA session
Article Text:
India reaffirms commitment to peaceful nuclear technology at UNGA, highlights South-South cooperation (representative image)

Countries thank India for development assistance

IAEA highlights growing role of nuclear energy

India has reaffirmed its commitment to the safe, secure and peaceful uses of nuclear science and technology at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), highlighting the role of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in promoting sustainable development and strengthening institutional capabilities.Sangeeta Kumari Singh Deo, Member of Parliament and leader of the Indian Parliamentary Delegation, addressed the General Assembly on the report of the IAEA, underlining the agency's role in helping member states develop human and institutional capacities, including regulatory frameworks for the peaceful application of nuclear science.In a post on X, India's mission to the UN said Singh Deo highlighted India's advancements in nuclear technology and its support for the IAEA's Technical Cooperation Programme and flagship initiatives.The mission also said India had reiterated its commitment to South-South cooperation to ensure that the benefits of nuclear science reach countries seeking them, while maintaining robust nuclear safety and security frameworks.Separately, several countries acknowledged India's development assistance at the Ninth Annual India-UN Development Partnership Fund event held on October 22.Representatives from Laos, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Micronesia, Moldova, Morocco and Saint Lucia were among those expressing appreciation for India's support.Moldova's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Gheorghe Leuca, said the partnership had strengthened the country's ability to use population data to improve public policies.“At a time of ODA strain, India's sustained committment sends an important message: ‘Partnership built on solidarity, mutual respect and national priorities can continue to deliver tangible results,’” Leuca said.Sri Lanka's UN envoy, ambassador Jayantha Jayasuriya, said the India-UN Fund addressed diverse thematic areas and supported projects based on the needs identified by participating countries.“The India-UN Fund caters to diversified thematic structures and these projects respond to needs identified by the countries themselves... its underlying philosophy is that respect for national priorities matters,” he said.Laos' UN ambassador, Thongphane Savanphet, commended India's role in advancing cooperation among developing countries.“We commend the Govt of India for the vital role in promoting the South-South cooperation. The India-UN Fund serves as an example of solidarity and partnership among developing countries, in supporting national development priorities. India has also extended its general support for our national priorities through other cooperation mechanisms,” he said.Tanzania's representative to the UN, ambassador Togolani Edriss Mavura, also expressed appreciation for India's continued support for sustainable development in the country.“Tanzania expresses its sincere appreciation to India and the India-UN Fund for their continued support for sustainable development in Tanzania,” he said.A representative of Morocco's delegation praised India's role in the initiative, saying: “We commend India's vision and generosity, as well as the UN Office of South-South Cooperation for its dedicated stewardship of this demand-driven initiative. Nearly a decade after its launch in 2017, the fund's record speaks for itself.”Mozambique's Permanent Representative to the UN, ambassador Domingos Estêvão Fernandes, said the fund demonstrated South-South cooperation based on national priorities, equality and non-interference, while complementing North-South cooperation.Meanwhile, IAEA director-general Rafael Grossi told the UN General Assembly that global nuclear power use could more than triple by 2060.Grossi said the projected growth would be driven by electrification, data centres powered by artificial intelligence and technology companies' demand for reliable, carbon-free electricity.“In 2025, more than 400 operating reactors in more than 30 countries produced 10 per cent of global electricity and a quarter of its low-carbon electricity,” Grossi said. He added that more than 60 new reactors were under construction and projections for future nuclear capacity had increased significantly.Grossi also addressed nuclear programmes in Iran and North Korea, threats to nuclear safety linked to the war in Ukraine, and progress in clarifying questions about Syria's nuclear activities.On Iran, he called for renewed diplomatic efforts and said IAEA inspectors needed to return to the country to support verification under any sustainable agreement.
Article Summary: India reaffirms commitment to peaceful nuclear technology at UNGA, highlights South-South cooperation.Countries thank India for development assistance. IAEA director-general Rafael Grossi told the UN General Assembly that global nuclear power use could more than triple by 2060.

Article Title: Brics parliamentary meet should end with joint statement: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla

NEW DELHI: The 12th Brics Parliamentary Forum that India will host on Oct 26-27 is expected to see participation from member-states like Russia, Iran, China, Brazil and the UAE. Iran will be represented by Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf.According to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, the forum marks a new chapter in the history of India’s parliamentary diplomacy.Talking to reporters Friday, Birla said the forum in India would work towards consensus-based dialogue on the role of Parliament in strengthening institutions, promotion of human-centred innovation in AI and digital technologies through Parliament, more representative system of global governance and role of Parliament in ensuring a sustainable and inclusive future for Brics countries.The meeting will take place against the continued hostilities in the West Asia region. While that issue is not a part of the official agenda, participants may choose to discuss the conflict on the sidelines. Despite the differences between Iran and the UAE, the Brics summit in India last month had concluded with a unanimous declaration.A meeting of the secretaries of the delegations will be held on Oct 25 to finalise a joint statement for the 12th Brics Parliamentary Forum, according to the Lok Sabha Speaker.West Asia tensions are unlikely to block the declaration. “India’s Parliament also holds discussions and engages in dialogue with all countries to build consensus. I hope that, with the agreement of all countries, there will be a joint declaration at the Brics Parliamentary Forum as well,” Birla said Thursday.
Article Summary: The 12th Brics Parliamentary Forum that India will host on Oct 26-27 is expected to see participation from member-states like Russia, Iran, China, Brazil and the UAE. According to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, the forum marks a new chapter in the history of India’s parliamentary diplomacy.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A parliamentary panel has called for “intercensal surveys” -- surveys between two successive censuses -- in India considering that cities and urban settlements undergo major changes in 10 years, and has also recommended review of the criteria for notifying “census towns” to make it more gender inclusive.At present, to qualify an urban area to be a census town, 75% male main working population must engage in non-agricultural activities. As per Census Commissioner of India, the proportion of female workers engaged in non-agricultural activities is not used as a criteria for classifying ‘census towns’ because female workforce participation fluctuates significantly due to social factors, under-reporting, and the informal nature of the work.The parliamentary standing committee on housing and urban affairs has recommended that this criteria is “based on a male-centric understanding of work and does not adequately reflect the growing participation of women in economic activities”. The panel added, “It also fails to capture the contribution of women engaged in self-employment, informal work, home-based work, service sector activities and other forms of employment that are often undercounted.It has highlighted how female labour force participation has been steadily increasing and labour force participation rate for persons aged 15 years and above stood at 34.8% in Aug, 2026. “In this context, continuing with a criterion based exclusively on male main workers would not reflect the changing socio-economic realities of India,” the panel said.The panel, in its report, has referred to a ministry’s suggestion for introduction of periodic intercensal surveys to capture rapid changes in urbanisation and emerging settlement patterns, as well as to address data gaps in the targeting, implementation and monitoring of various schemes and programmes.It has recommended the ministry, in consultation with the Office of Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (ORGI) and other ministries and departments concerned to examine the feasibility of instituting periodic intercensal surveys for capturing changes in urbanisation, emerging settlement patterns and other relevant urban indicators.ORGI had informed the panel that its primary mandate is to conduct the census and discharge related statutory functions while adding that proposal for conducting periodic intercensal surveys to capture rapid urban changes is a policy matter which may be examined separately by govt.The committee has also recommended the ministry to engage with states and UTs after the release of Census 2027 data to examine the feasibility of converting eligible census towns into statutory urban local bodies, while maintaining an updated database of their status.
Article Summary: At present, to qualify an urban area to be a census town, 75% male main working population must engage in non-agricultural activities. The parliamentary standing committee on housing and urban affairs has recommended that this criteria is ‘based on a male-centric understanding of work’

NEW DELHI: The Akhil Bharatiya Gurjar Mahasabha has raised concerns over what it describes as inadequate political and institutional representation of the Gurjar community, claiming that the community has only 20 MLAs among approximately 4,600 legislators in the country and no representation in the Union Cabinet.The organisation said the issue of representation would be a key focus of its national convention at Delhi’s Talkatora Stadium on October 27, where it plans to discuss political participation, reservation-related demands, youth development and social reform.Addressing a press conference at the Press Club of India on Friday, Mahasabha national president Harish Chandra Bhati called for greater representation of the community in political and institutional decision-making, including legislatures, the Supreme Court and the media.Bhati said the community’s contribution to the freedom struggle had not received adequate recognition and called for measures to address the historical and social consequences of the British-era Criminal Tribes Act. He said the law had branded members of the Gurjar community as criminals, contributing to displacement and long-term social exclusion.The representation figures cited by Bhati were claims made by the organisation and were not independently verified.Bhati said political support should be linked to the community receiving an appropriate share in decision-making. He indicated that the Mahasabha would discuss whether the community should reconsider its approach to supporting political parties without adequate representation.The convention will also consider a proposal to establish a separate political platform for the community. Bhati said the organisation would decide its future course after discussions at the gathering, for which it has estimated a turnout of around one lakh people.He also said the Mahasabha would raise the demand for a Gurjar Regiment in the armed forces, arguing that the community’s contribution to the country should receive greater recognition.The organisation said it would pursue its demands through democratic and constitutional means.The Mahasabha also called for the implementation of recommendations made by the Idate Commission, a revision of the base year for the caste census and the inclusion of Most Backward Classes (MBC) reservation provisions in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution.It further sought the withdrawal of cases related to Gurjar reservation that, according to the organisation, had remained pending for nearly 20 years.National organisation secretary Dr Roop Singh called for the identification and protection of historical sites associated with Gurjar-Pratihar-era rulers. He urged the Archaeological Survey of India to ensure their preservation and called for identification and information boards to be reinstalled at the sites.The October 27 convention will also discuss education, skill development, employment and greater participation of young people in public service.National vice-president Savinder Singh Bhati said the Mahasabha was running an initiative to encourage young people to express their views through peaceful, democratic and constitutional means, while discouraging violence and damage to public property. He also called for guidance and support for young people preparing for competitive examinations, including the IAS and IPS examinations.Another national vice-president, K P Singh Kasana, called for greater awareness about substance abuse and more opportunities for young people through skill development, employment guidance and links with industry.The organisation also plans to adopt resolutions against dowry demands and extravagant wedding spending, as well as costly post-death feasts that it says place financial pressure on families.The convention, being held to mark the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is expected to bring together community representatives from different states to discuss political representation, social reform and the future direction of the organisation.

NEW DELHI: Haryana’s striking electricity employees on Friday called off their three-day strike following a meeting with chief minister Nayab Singh Saini and power minister Anil Vij.The employees said Saini assured them that private players would not be allowed to enter Haryana’s power sector and that parallel power distribution licences would be revoked. NEW DELHI: A Delhi court on Friday allowed American mercenary Matthew Aaron VanDyke to travel to the United States and extended permission for six Ukrainian nationals to remain outside India until February 24.Special judge Prashant Sharma passed the order while hearing applications moved by the seven foreign nationals.VanDyke, along with the six Ukrainians, was arrested by the National Investigation Agency in March 2026 for allegedly providing weapons and drone-warfare training to ethnic armed groups in Myanmar.The court's decision came after the central probing agency submitted that it needed more time to investigate several aspects of the case. It's all ongoing. Especially now that I'm my own lawyer. I don't want to talk about it. There is a money issue. That's the main issue," he said.The NIA had alleged that VanDyke and the six Ukrainian nationals entered India on tourist visas, travelled to the northeastern region without mandatory permits and subsequently crossed from Mizoram into Myanmar, where they allegedly trained ethnic armed organisations.The agency had initially invoked provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), including those relating to conspiracy.It had also alleged that the accused disclosed details about the network and were involved in assembling equipment and targeting a passenger aircraft in Myanmar.However, in its charge sheet, the NIA did not invoke the UAPA provisions and instead proceeded under Sections 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, which provide for offences that can be compounded before the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO).The agency had earlier indicated that its investigation into the alleged terror-related aspects was continuing and that further allegations could be included in a supplementary charge sheet.

Article Title: 'Can't drive into future looking at rearview mirror': India calls for urgent UNSC reforms
Article Text:

India has called for urgent reforms to the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), warning that its 80-year-old structure is struggling to address some of the world’s gravest conflicts. New Delhi said the Council’s composition must reflect present-day global realities, arguing that its post-Second World War framework no longer adequately represents the international community.According to news agency PTI, India’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, said on Thursday that the authority inherited from the Second World War could no longer compensate for the Council’s lack of representative membership.“The cost is already visible. Eighty years on, the Organisation is struggling to deliver peace and reconciliation in some of the gravest conflicts before the Council,” Parvathaneni said while addressing the UN General Assembly on equitable representation and an expansion of the Security Council.He added that “the authority derived from a victory eight decades ago cannot compensate for the deficit in legitimacy of an unrepresentative Security Council today.”The Indian envoy argued that 1945, when the UN was established after the Second World War, could not remain the sole reference point for global governance.“No war, especially one that took place over 80 years ago, should determine today’s state of the world,” he said.“History can be a guide for what not to do. It cannot determine today’s choices for what needs to be done to face contemporary challenges. We cannot reasonably drive into the future by constantly looking at the rearview mirror,” he added.Parvathaneni also highlighted India’s contribution to the World Wars, arguing that the sacrifices of several nations had not received adequate recognition in the post-war international order.“An organisation crafted of the victors, for the victors and by the victors did not, obviously, care to include the concerns of the victims,” he said, calling for the Security Council to evolve “for the sake of its own relevance”.According to PTI, he noted that around 2.5 million Indians participated in the Second World War, with approximately 90,000 dying in military service. He also referred to the Bengal famine, which he attributed to colonial wartime policies.India further pointed to the under-representation of Asia-Pacific, Africa and Latin America. The Asia-Pacific region accounts for more than 60 per cent of the world’s population but has only one permanent seat on the Council, alongside a fluctuating elected representation.“Reform is not the settlement of old scores. It is an investment in a Council that all Member States can trust, and which would be stronger as a result,” Parvathaneni said.The 15-member UNSC comprises five permanent members — China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States — with veto powers, alongside 10 elected members serving two-year terms.India supports expanding both permanent and non-permanent membership, arguing that changes limited to elected seats would leave the central imbalance intact.Criticising the pace of negotiations, Parvathaneni said, “That is not negotiation; it is merely perpetuation of status quo.”He added, “Convergences are not consensus, and the search for a lowest common denominator must not become an excuse for cosmetically tinkering with the existing structure while calling it reform.”India also maintained that any permanent membership expansion must address the veto question fairly. “A two-tier permanent membership would only institutionalise inequality,” he said.
Article Summary: India has called for urgent reforms to the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) New Delhi said the Council’s composition must reflect present-day global realities. The 15-member UNSC comprises five permanent members with veto powers, alongside 10 elected members serving two-year terms.

Kapoor said the ITBP was building underground shelters in border areas to reduce vulnerabilities in the event of a conflict, as above-ground structures could become targets during a war.The force is also upgrading troop facilities in high-altitude areas, including insulating barracks, installing solar water heaters and providing generator sets to ensure electricity at remote posts. NEW DELHI: The Cabinet Secretariat did not take any action on complaints filed by two election commissioners against an officer in the Election Commission, saying the letters were written in their “individual capacity” and did not represent the poll panel as a whole, according to documents released in response to an RTI application.Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had separately written to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan on July 29, raising concerns about the conduct of senior deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg, an IAS officer appointed to the Commission by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) on September 2, 2024.The letters were provided in an RTI response to activist Commodore Lokesh K Batra (retd).The Indian Express had reported in September that the two Election Commissioners approached the Cabinet Secretary after Garg issued a work allocation order that they believed could concentrate powers over changes to voter records at the central level, instead of allowing officials at the state level to handle them.In a statement on September 26, the Election Commission said the work allocation orders issued by Garg were never implemented following directions from the two Commissioners.The poll panel also said the complaints concerned an officer on deputation and not matters related to policy or the IT division.According to a Cabinet note included in the RTI response, both Commissioners alleged that Garg had issued an order changing the work allocation of officers senior or equivalent to him after taking charge as the link officer of the deputy election commissioner (Administration).The Commissioners said the changes were made without consulting the Commission or the officers concerned. They also alleged that Garg acted despite repeated oral and written instructions against making such changes without prior discussion or approval from the Commission."Both the ECs have stated that Shri Garg, after assuming the charge as link officer of DEC (Admn), has issued an order regarding work allocation of equivalent and senior officers to him without discussing the revised work allocation with the Commission or the officers concerned. Further, the aforementioned ECs have stated that this has happened despite repeated oral and written instructions to all concerned officers against taking such actions without prior discussion/approval of the Commission," the Cabinet note said.The two Commissioners alleged that Garg's actions violated the chief election commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.Joshi also said that when he sought the relevant file from the Administration Division, it was not provided to him.A Cabinet note prepared on August 3 proposed seeking the chief election commissioner's opinion on the complaints."In this connection, we may request the chief election commissioner for his opinion on the issue. Accordingly, a draft DO is put up for approval, please."However, a subsequent note dated August 4 said taking action on complaints from individual Election Commissioners without an official communication from the Commission as a whole could be seen as interference in the functioning of the constitutional body."The Commission is a Constitutional Body and is insulated from executive interference by design to ensure that it functions independently and in a transparent manner. The working and functioning of the Commission are governed by the rules and guidelines of the Election Commission. The above communications are from the Election Commissioners in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from the Commission as a whole," the note said.It added that although Garg had been appointed by the ACC, he was now an officer of the Election Commission, and his work and conduct were governed by the poll panel's rules and guidelines.The note also referred to Section 18 of the 2023 Act, which states that the Commission should conduct its business unanimously as far as possible, with any differences of opinion settled by a majority decision."Election Commissioners have sent these communications for appropriate action; however, in the absence of any official communication from the Commission as a whole, any action at this stage may be inappropriate. It may also be construed as interference in the functioning of the Constitutional Body. Hence, it would be appropriate to send acknowledgement to both Election Commissioners with a copy to PPS to CEC for information of CEC," the note said.The draft note signed by Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan was also marked to the secretary of the department of personnel and training and the establishment officer to keep the matter on record.The note said this would "enable it to be taken into account in future decision-making regarding the officer".Somanathan also signed an acknowledgement letter confirming receipt of the complaints and sent copies to both election commissioners.The letters were acknowledged on August 5, 2026, with copies marked to the department of personnel and training, the Establishment Officer and the office of the chief election commissioner.
Article Summary: Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had separately written to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan on July 29. They had raised concerns about the conduct of senior deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg. The Cabinet Secretariat did not take any action on complaints filed by two election commissioners against an officer.

Article Title: Will back all meaningful efforts for Ukraine peace, PM Modi assures Poland's Tusk
Article Text:
PM Modi with Polish counterpart Donald Tusk at Hyderabad House Thursday.

Poll Vote & Share your view Should India and Poland strengthen their cooperation in defence and security? Strongly agree Somewhat agree Somewhat disagree Strongly disagree 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Looking to further expand their strategic partnership, India and Poland agreed to double bilateral trade by 2030 and announced dialogue mechanisms for defence industrial collaboration and counterterrorism cooperation as PM Narendra Modi hosted his counterpart Donald Tusk for talks Thursday.Modi and Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace.Poland views the war in Ukraine as a direct threat to its national security and sovereignty due to its shared border, influx of refugees and the threat of future Russian aggression in eastern Europe.“They reiterated the need for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in line with international law, consistent with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, including respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity,” said the joint statement. The leaders also noted the negative impacts of the war on global food and energy security, especially for the Global South.Modi and Tusk, the first Polish PM to visit India in 16 years, also backed an MoU under negotiation for cooperation in critical minerals.Modi said the friendship between India and Poland was based not only on diplomatic ties but also on a shared heritage of humanity and empathy. He recalled how, during the Second World War, the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur had provided shelter in India to thousands of Polish children and families. He also thanked Poland for helping India evacuate Indian students from Ukraine shortly after the Russia-Ukraine war began in 2022.Modi said the world was passing through a period of uncertainty and change, and even in such times, both India and Poland were emerging as important hubs of growth, technology and innovation.“Today we have agreed to deepen ties in defence, space and nuclear energy. In all these strategic sectors, we invite Polish companies to engage in co-development and co-production with India,” he said.He also announced a startup bridge to facilitate cooperation in IT, Artificial Intelligence and critical technologies.“Both India and Poland believe in democratic values and the rule of law,” Modi said, underlining that both sides considered reforms essential to make global governance institutions more empowered.The two countries agreed that the UN needed structural reforms, including expansion of UNSC in both permanent and non-permanent categories, to remain relevant, credible and effective. In the joint statement, Poland expressed support for India’s membership of a more inclusive, reformed and expanded UNSC, as well as its candidature for a non-permanent seat on the council for 2028-29.Modi and Tusk unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, and stressed that there could be no justification for terrorism on any grounds.“They condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in J&K’s Pahalgam on 22 April, 2025. They called for strong and concerted action against terrorists and terrorist entities, including those designated by the UNSC 1267 sanctions committee,” said the joint statement.Defence and security cooperation was a major focus, with the leaders underlining importance of an Agreement on Mutual Protection and Exchange of Classified Information and expressing expectation it would be signed soon.They proposed a defence industry dialogue to develop a “forward-looking framework for defence industrial cooperation”, including business-to-business engagement and, where mutually agreed, partnerships in technology, co-development, co-production and other forms of collaboration.
Article Summary: Poland views the war in Ukraine as a direct threat to its national security and sovereignty. PM Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace. Poland expressed support for India’s membership of a more inclusive, reformed and expanded UNSC.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.
