Article Title: Haryana power cut: Homes in dark for hours, residents block roads; factories stay shut for days, owners count their losses
Article Text:
Image Credit: X

What happens next?

Factories stay shut for days, owners count their losses





GURGAON: The power strike that crippled the city and other parts of Haryana for two days was called off late on Friday evening after chief minister Nayab Singh Saini assured electricity department employees that no private parallel power distribution licences would be allowed anywhere in the state.The shutdown had left many homes facing long outages and disrupted water supply, while bringing industrial production to a halt for more than 24 hours. Govt invoked Section 108(1) of Electricity Act, 2003 - which empowers it to issue policy directions to the state electricity regulator on matters of public interest - and asked it not to create or operationalise such licences.The order came four days after Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) granted Eleven Power Pvt Ltd a 25-year licence to distribute electricity alongside Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (DHBVN) in Gurgaon and Nuh.Representatives of Haryana Joint Action Committee said Saini and energy minister Anil Vij heard them out and apprised them of the steps being taken by govt to oppose the granting of parallel licences.The state said it was not questioning the correctness of HERC's findings in its order, but raised concerns over the private company's financial capacity, technical preparedness and ability to supply all consumers in its licensed area.It also flagged the risk of a private distributor choosing high-revenue consumers, potentially weakening cross-subsidy arrangements and leaving the state utility with existing power purchase commitments, stranded costs and duplicated infrastructure. These could increase the financial burden on DHBVN and consumers. The govt asked the HERC secretary to place the directive before the commission.Chief minister Saini also ordered officials to restore electricity immediately in all affected districts. Following his directions, Haryana Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Ltd (HVPNL) managing director Aditya Dahiya and DHBVN and Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam (UHBVN) managing director Vikram Singh met superintending and executive engineers and directed them to ensure uninterrupted supply.The strike had caused widespread disruption before the settlement. Outages stretched beyond 40 hours in some neighbourhoods, residents blocked Gurgaon-Pataudi Road, Railway Road and Basai Road, bringing traffic to a standstill until cops intervened. Water shortages, exhausted inverters and disrupted work routines added to the distress.Old Gurgaon bore much of the brunt, particularly colonies along Railway Road and Basai Road. In Ashok Vihar Phase 1, power went off on Thursday morning and remained unavailable in most homes until late Friday. Rajendra Park and Vishnu Garden reported outages from 10am on Thursday, while residents of Surat Nagar faced similar conditions. Hundreds of homes in sectors 4, 7 and 7 Extension, as well as New Palam Vihar, Sai Kunj and Chandan Vihar, reported prolonged cuts.The disruption also crippled water supply as electric pumps stopped working. In Hari Nagar on Khandsa Road, residents protested outside the Sector 34 power house on Thursday night after supply failed on Wednesday.DHBVN received around 9,500 complaints through its toll-free number over two days, including about 4,500 on Friday. By Friday evening, 32 feeders were still reported shut. Each feeder serves an average of 1,700 households, highlighting the scale of the problem.Several societies switched to generator power, which residents said cost around Rs 30 per unit. These included Hero Homes in Sector 104, Godrej Frontier in Sector 80, Chintels Paradiso in Sector 109 and Emerald Hills among others.Prolonged generator use also raised concerns about pollution.Affordable housing societies without generator backup suffered especially badly. Inverters ran out, water purifiers stopped working and families turned to bottled water. Santosh Singh of Pareena Laxmi Apartments in Sector 99A, home to around 650 families, said power had been unavailable since 6pm on Thursday.The industrial belt took a massive hit from three days of power cuts, with industry leaders estimating production losses of more than Rs 20,000 crore.Textile, auto components and food units, along with export houses, halted operations as outages disrupted manufacturing schedules, delayed customer orders and put delivery commitments at risk. Businesses also warned of damage to machinery and raw materials, while thousands of daily wagers lost earnings during the festive season.The strike was called off late on Friday evening after talks between employee representatives and energy minister Anil Vij. The disruption, however, had already hit production schedules, delayed customer orders and put delivery commitments at risk.Two industry bodies — Gurgaon Chamber of Commerce & Industry (GCCI) and Progressive Federation of Trade & Industry (PFTI) — wrote to chief minister Nayab Singh Saini, seeking urgent intervention to restore power and limit further losses.In its letter on Friday, GCCI said outages that began on the night of Oct 21 had severely affected industrial and commercial activity. Units were unable to maintain scheduled operations or meet customer deadlines, adding to the financial burden of lost production.The chamber also warned that interruptions could have consequences beyond the immediate loss of output. Sensitive machinery, production processes and raw materials could be damaged by power disruptions, while missed dispatch deadlines could affect contractual commitments.Some businesses tried using diesel generator (DG) sets, but GCCI said this was neither economical nor technically feasible over an extended period. Higher fuel bills added to operating costs, while generator capacity and technical limitations prevented many units from running their entire electrical load continuously.GCCI urged the state govt and power authorities to prioritise industrial feeders, manufacturing clusters and critical commercial areas. It also sought emergency contingency arrangements, better coordination among officials and reliable updates on restoration timelines so businesses could plan production and dispatches.PFTI, in a letter dated Oct 22, said the strike had left industrial operations stalled and workers idle in several areas. The timing had made matters worse. Businesses and workers usually depend on the festive season for higher production, earnings, incentives and bonuses.
Article Summary: The shutdown had left many homes facing long outages and disrupted water supply. It also brought industrial production to a halt for more than 24 hours. Chief minister Nayab Singh Saini assured electricity department employees that no private parallel power distribution licences would be allowed anywhere in the state. The order came four days after Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission granted Eleven Power Pvt Ltd a 25-year licence.

Article Title: Diljit Dosanjh's Delhi gig gets police nod amid fresh threats
Article Text:
With security concerns arising, the Delhi Police initially refused to grant permission for Diljit Dosanjh's upcoming concert

Cops advise organisers to coordinate with cab aggregators





NEW DELHI: A day after denying permission over "specific threat-related inputs" and security concerns, Delhi Police Friday cleared Diljit Dosanjh's concert, scheduled to be held at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on Oct 30.The nod came on a day when several Delhi schools received emails threatening that the singer's show would be targeted. A threat was received in Mumbai too, where he will perform on Nov 27.Police sources said the clearance was granted after organisers agreed to beef up arrangements for crowd management, deploy additional staff and coordinate with cops to ensure smooth conduct of the event.The organisers have been asked to increase their staff by about 1,500 personnel to assist with various arrangements at the venue, including crowd regulation and the management of entry and exit points. Police have also stressed the need for better coordination between the organisers and security personnel to prevent congestion and ensure attendees can enter and leave the stadium with-out inconvenience.Sources said the organisers have been directed to inform concertgoers in advance about parking facilities, traffic arrangements and designated drop-off and pick-up points. They have also been asked to encourage attendees to use the metro to reduce the number of private vehicles travelling to the venue.Police have also advised the organisers to coordinate with cab aggregators to stream-line pick-up and drop-off arrangements and prevent traffic congestion around the stadium. They have also been asked to tie up with navigation platforms to keep attendees informed about designated routes and traffic diversions.In a statement, BookMyShow said reports suggesting that Dosanjh’s concert in Delhi had been cancelled were inaccurate.“Permission for the event had been temporarily withheld, not cancelled, pending additional safety, traffic and crowd-management measures requested by Delhi Police in view of the festive season. BookMyShow Live has since held a cordial and constructive meeting with Delhi Police and presented a detailed plan addressing the required arrangements. We have assured the authorities of full compliance with all applicable security, traffic and crowd-management requirements,” the statement read.
Article Summary: Diljit Dosanjh's concert scheduled to be held at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on Oct 30. Delhi Police initially refused to grant permission over "specific threat- related inputs" and security concerns. Police sources said the clearance was granted after organisers agreed to beef up arrangements for crowd management.

Article Title: Delhi court orders trial of Yasin Malik, Engineer Rashid among 7 in Rs 8.94 crore money laundering case linked to hawala funding from Pakistan
Article Text:
Delhi court orders trial of Yasin Malik, Engineer Rashid, 5 others

Yasin Malik, Engineer Rashid among 7 accused

ED alleges Pakistan funding





NEW DELHI: A court in New Delhi has ordered a trial against jailed separatist leader Yasin Malik, Baramulla MP Sheikh Abdul Rashid, alias Engineer Rashid, and five others in a Rs 8.94 crore money laundering case linked to alleged funding from Pakistan through hawala channels for secessionist activities in Jammu and Kashmir.Special Judge Prashant Sharma ordered the framing of charges against the seven accused under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), observing that the material on record raised strong suspicion of their involvement in the offence.The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has alleged that proceeds of crime worth Rs 8.94 crore were generated and received by the accused and subsequently routed, transferred, concealed, possessed, acquired and used through various channels.The accused include Malik, chief of the banned Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF); separatist leader Shabir Ahmad Shah; Baramulla MP Sheikh Abdul Rashid, alias Engineer Rashid; Masarat Alam; Zahoor Ahmad Shah Watali; Naval Kishore Kapoor; and M/s Trison Farms and Constructions Pvt Ltd.The ED's case stems from a 2017 case registered by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), in which charges were invoked under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).The prosecution has alleged that the accused received funds from the "Pakistani establishment" through hawala channels and other means to promote secessionist activities and carry out acts prejudicial to the law of the land.According to the ED, the money was moved through a complex network of cash couriers and intermediaries who allegedly collected funds from the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi and delivered them to separatist leaders, including Malik, for subversive activities.The agency has alleged that Malik received foreign funds worth more than Rs 3 crore and laundered the proceeds of crime. It has also accused Shah and Rashid of receiving funds through intermediaries and maintaining links with separatist organisations.The allegations are yet to be established through trial.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: A court in New Delhi has ordered a trial against jailed separatist leader Yasin Malik, Baramulla MP Sheikh Abdul Rashid, alias Engineer Rashid. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has alleged that proceeds of crime worth Rs 8.94 crore were generated and received by the accused. The ED's case stems from a 2017 case registered by the National Investigation Agency.

Article Title: CM Devendra Fadnavis announces mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port, seeks Centre’s nod for 2,500-5,000 acres in Maharashtra

Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has revealed plans for a significant chemical park adjacent to Vadhvan Port





MUMBAI: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has announced plans for a mega chemical park near Vadhvan Port and urged the Centre to approve the project, for which the state government is willing to allot between 2,500 and 5,000 acres.Speaking at the inauguration of Indochem in Goregaon, Fadnavis said the state government would make the land available for the proposed park and asked the Centre to sanction the project.The proposed location is significant as Dahanu taluka in Palghar district was previously designated an ecologically sensitive zone.Union minister for chemicals and fertilisers JP Nadda said the Centre had already announced the Bhavya Rasayan scheme in the Union Budget. Under the scheme, the Centre will provide Rs 1,000 crore, while the state government will contribute Rs 500 crore.Nadda said the Centre would facilitate environmental clearances for the scheme.The proposed initiative is part of the Centre’s Viksit Bharat vision and its goal of building a $1 trillion economy by 2040.

Article Title: CBI arrests SFIO deputy director, advocate in Rs 1 crore bribe case linked to DHFL scam probe
Article Text:
The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. (Representative image)





CHENNAI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested a deputy director-level officer of the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO), Ministry of Corporate Affairs, posted in Chennai, a Delhi-based advocate and the advocate’s relative for allegedly demanding a Rs 1 crore bribe to favour a complainant in an investigation into the DHFL scam.The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch who is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai, advocate Bharat Sharma of New Delhi, and Aryan Sharma, a relative of the advocate, after laying a trap. The arrests followed the advocate’s alleged receipt of Rs 20 lakh from the complainant as part payment of the demanded bribe on behalf of the SFIO officer.According to the CBI, the case was registered against Tanwar, the advocate and others following allegations that they had demanded Rs 1 crore from the complainant to allegedly favour him in an investigation into the DHFL scam being conducted by the SFIO.The CBI verified the complaint before registering the case on Tuesday. It subsequently laid a trap and arrested the three accused after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant on behalf of the SFIO officer.The CBI also conducted searches at the premises of the public servant and the advocate and recovered incriminating material related to the case.The case has been registered under Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, relating to criminal conspiracy, and Sections 7 and 7A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Article Summary: The CBI arrested Harish Kumar Tanwar, an Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer of the 2017 batch. Tanwar is currently posted as deputy director of the SFIO in Chennai. The CBI laid a trap after the advocate allegedly received Rs 20 lakh from the complainant.

Article Title: Google’s Ex-CEO Eric Schmidt sees China behind the US in the AI race by at least 6 months, but is still impressed by Chinese …
Article Text:
Eric Schmidt ‘If they’re six months behind, we’re already losing’

Google’s ex-CEO points to smuggled chips and AI distillation

AI is not a bubble, says Eric Schmidt

Price may matter more than performance

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says China trails the US in artificial intelligence by roughly six months, but he warns that the gap may not guarantee an American win. Talking about the intensifying global AI competition, Schmidt said that China is only about six months behind the US in AI capabilities. Along with this, he also warned that the country’s focus on making low-cost and free AI products could enable it to dominate the global adoption. Schmidt believes that if the Chinese AI companies continue to offer powerful AI models at little of no cost, then they could easily gain a huge and significant advantage in developing markets which will incur pressure on the business model of leading AI companies in the US.As reported by Benzinga, speaking on the In Good Company podcast hosted by Nicolai Tangen, CEO of Norges Bank Investment Management, Schmidt said China's position in the AI race is much stronger than many in the West may believe. He argued that even if Chinese AI firms remain slightly behind the technological frontier, their strategy of offering inexpensive or free AI services could help them win users at a global scale.“I don’t know that they will get ahead, but I will tell you that if they’re six months behind, then we’re already losing because their strategy is that the products are free,” Schmidt said.Schmidt noted that many Chinese AI models are either free or significantly cheaper than their Western counterparts.Combined with the growing popularity of open-weight models, this pricing strategy could make Chinese AI offerings particularly attractive in emerging economies where businesses and consumers may not be able to afford premium AI subscriptions.The former Google chief also discussed how China has rapidly reduced the AI gap despite US export restrictions on advanced semiconductor technology. Schmidt said some of China's progress may have been enabled by access to cutting-edge chips that the country was “not supposed to have,” suggesting that some hardware may have been “pilfered or smuggled” into the country.Another factor, he said, is the use of AI distillation techniques, in which developers query advanced AI systems and use the generated responses to train their own models. Such approaches, combined with software innovation, have helped Chinese companies narrow what was once viewed as a much larger technological gap.Schmidt has previously said that China was one to two years behind the US in AI development. He now believes the gap has shrunk to less than six months, highlighting the speed at which Chinese AI firms have progressedDespite growing concerns over the massive sums being invested in artificial intelligence, Schmidt dismissed suggestions that the industry is experiencing a speculative bubble. The technology investor, who owns a stake in Anthropic, argued that the sector's financial performance demonstrates real customer demand rather than hype-driven growth.Pointing to Anthropic's rapid expansion, Schmidt said the company has achieved revenue growth at a pace that exceeds what Google experienced during his tenure as CEO.“That’s real growth. It’s not fake. It’s real money, with real customers who are paying for something useful,” he said.Schmidt's comments come amid an increasingly common view in the AI industry that affordability could become a bigger competitive factor than having the absolute most advanced model. While frontier AI systems continue to grab headlines, many businesses are primarily interested in practical tools that deliver acceptable performance at a reasonable cost.To illustrate the point, Schmidt highlighted a WeChat AI agent developed by Tencent Holdings that can scan medicine packaging and quickly provide personalised guidance. The example, he said, shows how AI systems do not necessarily need to be the most sophisticated models available to deliver meaningful value to users.He added that businesses evaluating AI investments often compare the cost of adopting AI tools with the cost of hiring additional employees, making pricing a critical consideration for enterprise adoption.
Article Summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says China trails the US in artificial intelligence by roughly six months. But he warns that the gap may not guarantee an American win. Schmidt said China's focus on making low-cost and free AI products could enable it to dominate the global adoption.

Article Title: Snapchat billionaire Evan Spiegel and wife Miranda Kerr help erase $550 million in medical debt for 261,000 Californians struggling to pay bills, now turning to LA wildfire survivors
Article Text:
Image: Evan Spiegel/ Instagram

Snapchat billionaire helps erase $550 million in medical debt

Spiegel turns to Los Angeles wildfire recovery

Department of Angels supports wildfire survivors

Couple fund research into long-term health effects of the fires

Spiegel and Kerr involve their children in charitable work

Evan Spiegel honoured for philanthropy in Washington

Snapchat co-founder and Snap Inc. CEO Evan Spiegel and his wife, Australian model and entrepreneur Miranda Kerr, have helped erase $550 million in medical debt owed by more than 261,000 Californians. The couple made a multimillion-dollar donation to Undue Medical Debt, a nonprofit that purchases qualifying medical debt for a fraction of its original value before cancelling it. Their philanthropic efforts also extend to Los Angeles, where devastating wildfires in January 2025 destroyed thousands of structures, including Spiegel’s childhood home in Pacific Palisades. More than a year after the disaster, the couple continues to support recovery initiatives for affected residents and research into the fires’ long-term health consequences. Spiegel was honoured for his philanthropic work at an awards ceremony in Washington, DC, on October 13, 2026.Spiegel and Kerr’s medical debt relief initiative was announced in June 2026 and reported by the Los Angeles Times. Their contribution helped Undue Medical Debt cancel more than $550 million in outstanding medical bills for over 261,000 Californians.The nonprofit acquires medical debt in bulk from hospitals, physician groups, collection agencies and other creditors, often paying substantially less than the original amount owed.It then cancels the acquired debt, allowing eligible individuals to receive relief without having to repay the outstanding balance.According to the organisation, people generally qualify if their household income is at or below 400% of the federal poverty level or if their medical debt represents at least 5% of their annual income. Recipients do not need to apply individually because the nonprofit identifies and purchases qualifying debts in bulk.The $550 million figure represents the face value of the debt cancelled, rather than the amount donated by the couple. Their precise contribution has not been publicly disclosed.The initiative reached communities across California. San Diego County received approximately $99 million in medical debt relief, benefiting 40,369 people, while Los Angeles County saw $26.7 million in debt cancelled for 17,466 residents, according to figures reported by the Los Angeles Times.The couple’s philanthropy has also focused on communities devastated by the January 2025 wildfires in Los Angeles County. Spiegel grew up in Pacific Palisades, where his childhood home was destroyed during the disaster.The fires killed dozens of people and destroyed more than 16,000 structures, according to early assessments. The destruction left thousands of residents facing the lengthy process of securing assistance, assessing damage and rebuilding their homes.The disaster also affected Spiegel’s company. In an interview with PEOPLE published on October 15, 2026, he said more than 100 Snap employees had been affected by the fires.In January 2025, Spiegel, Snap and Snapchat co-founder Bobby Murphy contributed $5 million in immediate aid. The support formed part of a wider philanthropic response to the disaster.Recalling the moment he learnt that his childhood home was burning, Spiegel told PEOPLE that his sister alerted the family after seeing the house on television. He described the experience as surreal, particularly because the house was where he and Murphy had started Snapchat.Spiegel also helped launch the Department of Angels, a nonprofit established to support Los Angeles wildfire recovery. The California Community Foundation, Snap, Spiegel and Murphy committed a combined $10 million in seed funding to establish the initiative, the Los Angeles Times reported.The organisation works to connect affected residents with resources, support community-led recovery and bring survivors’ concerns to decision-makers at the local, state and federal levels.Its work comes as many residents continue to face obstacles in rebuilding their homes and returning to their neighbourhoods. In August 2026, The Guardian reported that thousands of wildfire survivors were still waiting for more than $15 billion in federal recovery assistance.Spiegel told PEOPLE that the delays remained frustrating and stressed that the recognition of his philanthropic work should not overshadow the needs of affected communities.Beyond immediate financial assistance, the Spiegel Family Fund supported the launch of the Los Angeles Fire Human Exposure and Long-Term Health Study, also known as the L.A. Fire HEALTH Study, in January 2025.The 10-year research initiative brings together scientists from institutions including UCLA, Harvard University, the University of California, Davis, and the University of Texas at Austin. Researchers are investigating pollutants released during the fires, how they spread through air, soil, dust and water, and the possible short- and long-term health consequences of exposure.The study also aims to provide evidence that can help residents understand the risks of returning to affected homes and neighbourhoods. Urban fires can burn synthetic materials, household products and building components, potentially releasing a complex mixture of pollutants.The findings could help communities better prepare for future urban wildfires and guide decisions about environmental monitoring and recovery. Researchers will need to follow exposed populations over time to establish the nature and extent of any lasting health effects.The couple have also sought to make community service part of family life. Spiegel and Kerr are raising three sons together, Hart, Myles and Pierre. Kerr also has a son, Flynn, from her previous marriage to actor Orlando Bloom.Speaking to PEOPLE, Spiegel said the family tries to involve their children in activities such as packing meals and baking cookies for a local women's shelter.He said he wants his children to understand that their opportunities come with a responsibility to help people who are less fortunate. Kerr, he added, has inspired him through her care for others since the early days of their relationship.Their philanthropic interests extend beyond medical debt and disaster recovery. In 2022, the couple helped pay off student loans for the graduating class at Otis College of Art and Design in Los Angeles. Spiegel's wider giving also includes support for creative education and opportunities for young people through the Spiegel Family Fund and the Snap Foundation.On October 13, 2026, Spiegel was honoured at the eighth annual George H.W. Bush Points of Light Awards in Washington, DC. The ceremony recognised individuals for their philanthropic work, volunteering and contributions to communities across the United States.Other honourees included David M. Rubenstein, co-founder of investment firm The Carlyle Group, and Olivia Zhang, founder and CEO of Cancer Kids First.Reflecting on the recognition, Spiegel told PEOPLE that he was grateful for what had been accomplished but believed it was important to acknowledge how much more work remained. He specifically pointed to wildfire survivors still waiting for federal assistance.He also spoke about the importance of helping others, describing people as interconnected and saying that this creates an obligation to support one another. For Spiegel and Kerr, their efforts span immediate financial relief for families burdened by medical bills and longer-term work to help communities recover from disasters.
Article Summary: Snap Inc. CEO Evan Spiegel and his wife Miranda Kerr have helped erase $550 million in medical debt owed by more than 261,000 Californians. The couple made a multimillion-dollar donation to Undue Medical Debt, a nonprofit that purchases qualifying medical debt for a fraction of its original value. Their philanthropic efforts also extend to Los Angeles, where devastating wildfires in January 2025 destroyed thousands of structures, including Spiegel’s childhood home.

Article Title: Microsoft shuts down its 17-year-old innovation lab where Satya Nadella came to see what employees were building; company says: "Spirit of experimentation is now reflected in how..."
Article Text:
FILE - The logo of Microsoft is seen outside its French headquarters in Issy-les-Moulineaux, outside Paris on May 13, 2024. (AP Photo/Thibault Camus, File)

Microsoft says The Garage will no longer run as a centralised program

Xbox Adaptive Controller and Seeing AI were born in Microsoft Garage hackathons

Employees link the Garage closure to Microsoft's wider cost cuts

Microsoft is shutting down The Garage, the companywide program that gave employees space and tools for side projects and ran its annual Global Hackathon. The move ends a 17-year run for an effort that started as a small Office Labs experiment in Redmond and grew into maker spaces across 15 regions, from Vancouver and New York to Israel, India and Beijing. GeekWire first reported the news, citing an internal FAQ, and some Garage spaces could be restricted starting Friday, October 23.The Garage mattered beyond its workbenches and soldering irons. CEO Satya Nadella was a regular at its hackathons, where employees could put their projects in front of senior executives. Now the internal FAQ tells staff that "the spirit of experimentation that once lived primarily in dedicated programs is now reflected in how teams work every day." Employees cannot take any equipment, tools or materials with them when the spaces close.According to the FAQ, The Garage will stop operating as a centralised function, and the impact on each location will vary. Neither the FAQ nor Microsoft has said which spaces are affected, including the flagship site in Redmond.A Microsoft spokesperson said the company regularly reviews how it uses its physical spaces and is making changes to some Garage locations.It declined to comment on what happens to Garage employees.The Global Hackathon's future is also unclear. The FAQ says the hackathon team is reimagining the event and will share more later. Microsoft's public Garage website, which showcased hackathon projects and experimental apps, now redirects to the company homepage.The Garage began in 2009 with the slogan "Doers. Not Talkers." Rather than collecting ideas and funding the popular ones, it backed employees who were already building things on their own. Its profile grew after Nadella became CEO in 2014. That July, it ran Microsoft's first companywide hackathon, which drew over 11,000 registrants from 80 countries.Several real products came out of it. Seeing AI, the app that describes objects and text for people who are blind or have low vision, started at a 2015 hackathon. The Xbox Adaptive Controller grew out of a hackathon project that used Kinect motion tracking. The controller was nearly cut over budget concerns before it shipped, The Verge’s Notepad newsletter noted, and went on to star in Microsoft’s 2019 Super Bowl ad. Employee Tuong Do built Mouse Without Borders, which lets one keyboard and mouse control up to four PCs, on evenings and weekends. Arrow Launcher, another Garage app, later became Microsoft Launcher for Android.The shutdown comes as Microsoft spends heavily on AI infrastructure such as data centres while cutting costs and jobs elsewhere. On Blind, the anonymous workplace app, a post titled "Amy kills the Garage" drew more than 70 comments, with the poster blaming CFO Amy Hood. One employee wrote that the space was where they met friends and made connections that helped their career.It is also the latest in a string of campus closures this year. In January, Microsoft shut its employee libraries in Redmond, Hyderabad, Beijing and Dublin, describing the shift as a move to an "AI-powered learning experience." Its Visitor Center in Redmond's Building 92 closed a month later.The FAQ thanks the employees, volunteers and partners who built The Garage and says Microsoft will carry its legacy forward in new forms. It does not say what those forms will be.
Article Summary: Microsoft is shutting down The Garage, the companywide program that gave employees space and tools for side projects. The move ends a 17-year run for an effort that started as a small Office Labs experiment in Redmond and grew into maker spaces across 15 regions. Employees cannot take any equipment, tools or materials with them when the spaces close.Xbox Adaptive Controller and Seeing AI were born in Microsoft Garage hackathons.
